findings.highlight: It's not like we're going for the fine arts or something
findings.evidenceJa: 本人たちは芸術のつもりか何だか知らねえけどさ
findings.explanation: Takeya says he does not know whether the music students themselves think what they are doing is art. The English changes the subject to “we” and turns his sneer at their self-conception into a statement about his own group.
findings.japanese:
「空気読んでねぇよなぁ。
本人たちは芸術のつもりか何だか知らねえけどさ」
findings.todokanai: "They're not seeing the big picture. It's not like we're going for the fine arts or something, y'know?"

findings.highlight: derail the conversation
findings.evidenceJa: いつの間に振りほどいた
findings.explanation: 振りほどいた means that Fujishiro physically shook off Takeya's grip. Nothing here means derailing a conversation.
findings.japanese:
「ああっ！？
いつの間に振りほどいた！？」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh!? When did you manage to derail the conversation!?"

findings.highlight: put a white flag on your grave
findings.evidenceJa: 草葉の陰から白旗くらいは振っててやる
findings.explanation: Fujishiro jokes that from beyond the grave he will at least wave a white flag of surrender. The translation instead puts the flag on Takeya's grave, reversing both whose grave is imagined and what happens to the flag.
findings.japanese:
「頑張ってくれ飯塚。成功を祈ってるぞ。
草葉の陰から白旗くらいは振っててやるからな」
findings.todokanai: "Hang in there, Iizuka. I'll be praying for your success. And I'll be sure to put a white flag on your grave!"

findings.highlight: Speak of the devil
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってる側から説教だし
findings.explanation: Takeya means “and you're lecturing me even as you say that.” “Speak of the devil” is the wrong English idiom: nobody has just appeared after being mentioned.
findings.japanese: 「言ってる側から説教だし」
findings.todokanai: "Speak of the devil, here it comes again…"

findings.highlight: as if to say she wouldn't allow anyone to get in her way
findings.evidenceJa: 誰が止めることができようか反語
findings.explanation: Takeya grandly asks who could stop her passion and then literally says “rhetorical question,” reading out the grammatical device as part of his evasive joke. The translation invents a claim about her refusing to be stopped and deletes the joke.
findings.japanese:
「自分の奥底にある想いを精一杯表現したいって情熱を
誰が止めることができようか反語…」
findings.todokanai: "The burning passion deep inside of her was just dying to burst out, as if to say she wouldn't allow anyone to get in her way…"

findings.highlight: was subject to her influence
findings.evidenceJa: その煽りを食らった
findings.explanation: 煽りを食らう means to suffer the adverse fallout from something. The neutral phrase “was subject to her influence” removes the consequence that destroyed the club.
findings.japanese: その煽りを食らったのが我らが軽音楽同好会。
findings.todokanai: Consequently, our light music club was subject to her influence.

findings.highlight: Every year, someone is nominated to be club president in order to gather volunteers in the three months leading up to the school festival.
findings.evidenceJa: 毎年、学園祭の三ヶ月前に集まる有志によって、脈々と受け継がれるこの適当な呼称を持つ当会
findings.explanation: The source says volunteers gather three months before the festival and perpetuate this loosely named organization from year to year. It says nothing about nominating a president to recruit them; that procedure is invented.
findings.japanese:
毎年、学園祭の三ヶ月前に集まる有志によって、
脈々と受け継がれるこの適当な呼称を持つ当会は、
今年は我がそこそこの友、飯塚武也によって旗揚げされた。
findings.todokanai: Every year, someone is nominated to be club president in order to gather volunteers in the three months leading up to the school festival. This year, it happened to be none other than my dearest friend, Iizuka Takeya.

findings.highlight: persuade and manipulate members who were not satisfied with her
findings.evidenceJa: 全員を自由自在に操ろうと画策していた
findings.explanation: She used any means necessary to win over the members who opposed her, then plotted to control everyone. The English makes only the dissatisfied members the object of both persuasion and manipulation.
findings.japanese:
彼女の加入を快く思わないメンバーを、
なりふり構わない手段で懐柔して、
全員を自由自在に操ろうと画策していた。
findings.todokanai: She did everything in her power to persuade and manipulate members who were not satisfied with her.

findings.highlight: the word "persuade" is definitely an understatement
findings.evidenceJa: 『懐柔』という言葉がぴったり来るくらいに柔らかそうだった
findings.explanation: The joke pivots from 懐柔, “to win someone over,” to the literal 柔, “soft”: whatever Tomo used on Haruki looked very soft indeed. Calling “persuade” an understatement neither conveys the physical insinuation nor forms an English joke.
findings.japanese:
…まさに『懐柔』という言葉が
ぴったり来るくらいに柔らかそうだった。
findings.todokanai: …Yeah, the word "persuade" is definitely an understatement.

findings.highlight: pull ourselves together somehow
findings.evidenceJa: 何が何でも形にしないと
findings.explanation: 形にする means they must produce a workable performance at any cost. “Pull ourselves together” means recover composure, not assemble the band or get the show into presentable form.
findings.japanese:
「もうエントリーは済んでるし、
プログラムも入稿寸前だし、
…何が何でも形にしないと」
findings.todokanai: "We've already signed up to perform at the festival, and the program has to be submitted shortly… We have to pull ourselves together somehow."

findings.highlight: another ten times
findings.evidenceJa: 残り１０回を切った
findings.explanation: They have fewer than ten uses of the room left, not another ten.
findings.japanese:
あと一月半…
ここで練習できるのも残り１０回を切ったところで、
事態は綺麗に無垢にまっさらに白紙に戻ってきた。
findings.todokanai: Only a month and a half left… Since we can only practice here another ten times, the situation really has devolved into a pure blank slate.

findings.highlight: if I had her popularity, good looks, and silver tongue
findings.evidenceJa: その人気と外見と媚び慣れた態度があれば
findings.explanation: Haruki is considering what the club could have achieved with Tomo and those assets at its disposal. The English instead imagines Haruki personally possessing her popularity, appearance, and manner.
findings.japanese:
それでも、その人気と外見と媚び慣れた態度があれば、
俺の目的は、結構な確率で達成されたんだろうけどな。
findings.todokanai: But even so, if I had her popularity, good looks, and silver tongue, I could probably achieve my goals rather easily as well.

findings.highlight: out of anyone else's sight
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も聞いていないのをいいことに
findings.explanation: Haruki takes advantage of nobody listening and sighs extravagantly. The translation changes an auditory circumstance into being outside everyone else's sight.
findings.japanese:
俺、峰城大付３年Ｅ組北原春希は、
誰も聞いていないのをいいことに、盛大なため息をついた。
findings.todokanai: I, Kitahara Haruki, of Houjou High School's Class 3-E, could only let out a deep sigh, out of anyone else's sight.

findings.highlight: since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name
findings.evidenceJa: まさに“付属した祭”
findings.explanation: The quoted phrase calls the school festival itself an “attached festival,” extending the joke in the school's 付属 designation to the event's subordinate scale. The English replaces the wordplay with an invented explanation about sharing the university's name.
findings.japanese:
近隣どころか県外からも多くの人が押し寄せる
峰城大祭に比べ、そりゃ悲しいほどの規模の差を誇る
まさに“付属した祭”なのは仕方のないところ。
findings.todokanai: The university's festival gets swarmed every year not only by local visitors but also by those from outside the prefecture. As such, it's a given that our own festival is pitifully small in comparison, since our high school is merely affiliated with and shares the university's name.

findings.highlight: cunningly placed signboards within the university
findings.evidenceJa: 向こうの看板イベントにあざといまでに便乗し
findings.explanation: 看板イベント means the university festival's flagship event. The high-school contest shamelessly piggybacks on it; there are no cunningly placed signboards.
findings.japanese:
中でも向こうの看板イベントにあざといまでに便乗し、
ある意味本家以上に“内輪で”盛り上がるのが、
この『ミス峰城大付属』。
findings.todokanai: Among other things, there are some cunningly placed signboards within the university, and in a sense, the enthusiasm surrounding the Miss Houjou High contest is greater than anything on the university campus. For us, anyway.

findings.highlight: We had to consider public criticism, the decisions made by staff
findings.evidenceJa: 世間の批判とかも考慮した職員側の判断もあり
findings.explanation: The staff made the decision after considering possible public criticism. The English makes the students the ones obliged to consider criticism and treats the staff's decision as a separate item on their list.
findings.japanese:
けれど、大学ほど自治権を認められていないしがない付属。
色々と世間の批判とかも考慮した職員側の判断もあり、
ミスコンの正式開催が理事会で通ることはなかった。
findings.todokanai: However, merely being affiliated with the university, we are not allowed to have the kind of autonomy which they hold. We had to consider public criticism, the decisions made by staff, and the fact that the school directors never formally approved the holding of our beauty pageant.

findings.highlight: the organizers of the school festival executive committee
findings.evidenceJa: 付属祭実行委員会を二段構えで組織して
findings.explanation: The upperclassmen organized the festival committee as a two-tier structure so the unauthorized contest could operate underneath the official body. The translation omits that mechanism and reduces them to generic committee organizers.
findings.japanese:
しかし、地下で燻っているような先輩諸兄では…
彼らは、付属祭実行委員会を二段構えで組織して、
めでたく『ミス峰城大付属』は裏開催される運びとなった。
findings.todokanai: And so, those upperclassmen that smoldered underground… they, the organizers of the school festival executive committee, opened up Miss Houjou High behind the scenes.

findings.highlight: a failure in the making
findings.evidenceJa: すでに付属祭の裏目玉として定着した趣がある
findings.explanation: The source says the unofficial contest has already become established as the festival's hidden attraction. The translation calls it a coming failure, reversing its status.
findings.japanese:
そんな華々しくない、学生側の自主規制と
学園側の黙認によって成り立っているイベントは、
すでに付属祭の裏目玉として定着した趣がある。
findings.todokanai: Given that it was hardly anything spectacular, the students' regulations and the campus' tacit consent had clued in that it was a failure in the making.

findings.highlight: In the late autumn The neighboring student does Not a single thing
findings.evidenceJa: 秋深し　隣はなにも　しない人
findings.explanation: This is a comic rewrite of the famous haiku 秋深き／隣は何を／する人ぞ: Haruki changes the wondering “What is my neighbor doing?” into “my neighbor does nothing.” The literal English leaves the allusion and the act of parody entirely invisible.
findings.japanese: 秋深し　隣はなにも　しない人
findings.todokanai: In the late autumn The neighboring student does Not a single thing

findings.highlight: sent a letter yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: それなら昨日通しといた
findings.explanation: Haruki says he got the rugby stall approved yesterday, then compiled the handover notes and gave them to the club president. No letter was sent.
findings.japanese:
「それなら昨日通しといた。
申し送り事項は全部まとめて部長に渡したから」
findings.todokanai: "I already sent a letter yesterday. Explaining all the details to the club president."

findings.highlight: I'm pretty sure saying this right now, seems really inexcusable
findings.evidenceJa: 今さらこんなこと言うの、本当に申し訳ないって思うんですけど
findings.explanation: The comma splits the subject from its verb and leaves “I'm pretty sure” without a coherent complement. This is not grammatical English.
findings.japanese:
「その、今さらこんなこと言うの、
本当に申し訳ないって思うんですけど…」
findings.todokanai: "Listen, I'm pretty sure saying this right now, seems really inexcusable…"

findings.highlight: I'm going to have to withdraw from the contest
findings.evidenceJa: 今年は辞退って訳には
findings.explanation: Setsuna tentatively asks whether withdrawing this year might be possible, trailing off before completing the request. The translation turns that hesitant question into a definite announcement that she must withdraw.
findings.japanese: 「わたし、今年は辞退って訳には…」
findings.todokanai: "This year, I'm going to have to withdraw from the contest…"

findings.highlight: make the request to the printing shop this coming Monday
findings.evidenceJa: 週明けで印刷所押さえといて
findings.explanation: Haruki tells her to secure or book the printer for the beginning of the week. The English instead tells her to wait until Monday and then make an unspecified request.
findings.japanese:
「それは今夜中にやっとくから。
もう週明けで印刷所押さえといて」
findings.todokanai: "It'll be finished tonight. You can make the request to the printing shop this coming Monday."

findings.highlight: Be sure to bring it tomorrow morning
findings.evidenceJa: 明日の午前中までに打ち出しといて
findings.explanation: She asks Haruki to print the material out by tomorrow morning. “Bring it” omits the required action.
findings.japanese:
「ありがと、恩に着る！
明日の午前中までに打ち出しといて」
findings.todokanai: "Thank you, I'm in your debt! Be sure to bring it tomorrow morning."

findings.highlight: Once I've worked out the details
findings.evidenceJa: 委細了解してるから
findings.explanation: Haruki says he already understands all the particulars. The English changes that completed understanding into something he has yet to work out.
findings.japanese:
「委細了解してるから。
…ごめん、また話の腰を折った」
findings.todokanai: "Once I've worked out the details… Sorry, I got distracted again."

findings.highlight: personally, or by proxy
findings.evidenceJa: 自薦・他薦を問わず
findings.explanation: 自薦・他薦 means self-nomination or nomination by someone else. “By proxy” means another person acts on the entrant's behalf, which is not the rule being described.
findings.japanese:
「エントリー条件には『自薦・他薦を問わず』とあるけど、
もちろん本人の合意が大前提だ。
小木曽が嫌だったら、エントリーは取り消す」
findings.todokanai: "The entry requirements state that people can enter 'personally, or by proxy,' but only with consent, of course. If you don't like it, Ogiso, we can revoke your entry."

findings.highlight: The way you can persuade someone just by turning your back to them.
findings.evidenceJa: その、背中で語る様に
findings.explanation: Chikashi says Haruki's dejected back speaks for itself; Haruki immediately asks whether he looks that crushed. The English invents a power to persuade people by turning his back.
findings.japanese:
「俺…お前を尊敬するわ。
その、背中で語る様に」
findings.todokanai: "I… seriously respect you, man. The way you can persuade someone just by turning your back to them."

findings.highlight: who's been in the class next to mine for the past two years
findings.evidenceJa: 二つ隣のクラスの同級生
findings.explanation: Takeya is a classmate in the class two over from Haruki's, not someone who has spent the past two years in the adjacent class.
findings.japanese:
そこで何の準備もせずに佇んでいたのは、
軽音楽同好会の部長と、二つ隣のクラスの同級生と、
腐れ縁の親友の一人だった。
findings.todokanai: This person loitering around without preparing for anything right nowーthe president of the Light Music Club, a student from the same grade who's been in the class next to mine for the past two yearsーis an inseparable friend of mine.

findings.highlight: one should never rely on Takeya to try to mend friendships destroyed over a woman
findings.evidenceJa: 友情が修復することは、経験上最初からアテにしていないはずの武也
findings.explanation: Takeya himself knows from experience not to expect friendships broken over a woman to repair themselves, so he searches for replacements. The translation instead says other people cannot rely on Takeya to repair them.
findings.japanese:
女がらみで崩壊した友情が修復することは、
経験上最初からアテにしていないはずの武也は、
どうやら新メンバーを探して奔走していたようだけど…
findings.todokanai: Speaking from experience, one should never rely on Takeya to try to mend friendships destroyed over a woman. However, there he was, running around trying to find new members…

findings.highlight: for reasons beyond my control
findings.evidenceJa: 主にどうしようもある理由で
findings.explanation: The joke says the poor result is mainly due to reasons that could be helped—Takeya's absurd standards. “Beyond my control” reverses that point and changes whose control is at issue.
findings.japanese:
まぁ、主にどうしようもある理由で
結果は芳しくないようだった。
findings.todokanai: Though, for reasons beyond my control, it seems it was pointless after all.

findings.highlight: Areyouevenaman!?
findings.evidenceJa: 潔っ
findings.explanation: Haruki starts an oddly clipped form of 潔い in reaction to how quickly Takeya gives up, prompting Takeya to question the pronunciation. Nothing in the source asks whether Takeya is a man.
findings.todokanai: "Areyouevenaman!?"

findings.highlight: Maybe I've just been discouraged by these long past two days.
findings.evidenceJa: 『最初から無理だったんだよ』って結論を出すのに、二日は長すぎたかもしれない
findings.explanation: Takeya says two days may already have been too long to reach the conclusion that it was impossible from the start. He does not say that two discouraging days caused his mood.
findings.japanese:
「『最初から無理だったんだよ』って結論を出すのに、
二日は長すぎたかもしれないな」
findings.todokanai: "The only conclusion I'm drawing is that it was hopeless from the start. Maybe I've just been discouraged by these long past two days."

findings.highlight: I've told you this before, Takeya
findings.evidenceJa: 前から言おうと思ってたんだけどな武也
findings.explanation: Haruki claims he has merely been meaning to say this for a while; Takeya's next line punctures the pose by saying Haruki has told him clearly many times. The English has Haruki concede that at once, destroying the retort.
findings.japanese:
「前から言おうと思ってたんだけどな武也…
今日こそはハッキリ言わせてもらうぞ」
findings.todokanai: "I've told you this before, Takeya… so I'll spell it out clearly for you today."

findings.highlight: I'm only participating in what I want to do.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ適当に参加してるだけだし
findings.explanation: Haruki minimizes his role as casual, halfhearted participation. He is not saying that he selectively participates only in activities he wants.
findings.japanese:
「俺は別に…
ただ適当に参加してるだけだし」
findings.todokanai: "I don't really mind… I'm only participating in what I want to do."

findings.highlight: That's also… something I do of my own volition.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなことは………自分の意志でやってることだし
findings.explanation: Haruki begins to deny Takeya's description—“That's not…”—but cannot complete it and retreats to saying he acts voluntarily. “That's also” removes the failed denial that the narration explicitly comments on.
findings.japanese:
「そんなことは………
自分の意志でやってることだし」
findings.todokanai: "That's also… something I do of my own volition."

findings.highlight: the festival committee, the executive committee
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭の表実行委員に、裏実行委員に
findings.explanation: Takeya contrasts the official festival committee with its underground counterpart. The English turns them into two generic committee names and loses the overt/covert joke.
findings.japanese:
「ウチらの手伝いだけじゃなく、
学園祭の表実行委員に、裏実行委員に、Ｗｅｂ担当に、
クラス委員と図書委員と…しかも全部ヘルプで」
findings.todokanai: "You're not only helping us, you're also doing things for the festival committee, the executive committee, being the admin of the school web page, being the class representative, even on the library committee… besides the fact that you're just lending a hand."

findings.highlight: he was being run ragged by girls
findings.evidenceJa: 女の子関係で便利に使い倒されることは
findings.explanation: Haruki says Takeya works him mercilessly whenever girls are involved, with roughly the frequency of eating and sleeping. The English makes Takeya the person being run ragged by the girls.
findings.japanese:
まぁ確かに女の子関係で便利に使い倒されることは、
それこそ人間の三大欲求の残り二つの頻度くらいに
発生する事態ではある訳だけど。
findings.todokanai: It's true that he was being run ragged by girls at about the same frequency as the other two primal urges.

findings.highlight: he wasn't like the people that had come and gone
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで色々とはっちゃけた人間じゃなくて
findings.explanation: Haruki says that until a year ago Takeya was not this uninhibited and over-the-top. The source contains no comparison with people who came and went.
findings.japanese:
それに、一年前までは、
ここまで色々とはっちゃけた人間じゃなくて…
findings.todokanai: And besides, up until last year, he wasn't like the people that had come and gone…

findings.highlight: That piano accompanied me many times, until I finally got into shape. And when it was pleased with my form, it accompanied my music.
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も何度もつっかえて、ようやく形になって、一人悦に入っていたとき、その伴奏は自然にやってきた
findings.explanation: Haruki is the one who repeatedly stumbles, finally gets the piece into shape, and sits alone enjoying his success when the accompaniment arrives. The English makes the piano accompany him throughout and then makes the piano pleased with his form.
findings.japanese:
何度も何度もつっかえて、ようやく形になって、
一人悦に入っていたとき、その伴奏は自然にやってきた。
findings.todokanai: That piano accompanied me many times, until I finally got into shape. And when it was pleased with my form, it accompanied my music.

findings.highlight: would pull pranks on me, guide me, and even show me my weaknesses
findings.evidenceJa: イタズラしているようにも、俺を導いてくれてるようにも、腕の違いを見せつけてるようにも聞こえる
findings.explanation: Haruki offers three alternative impressions of the sound: teasing him, guiding him, or showing off the gap in their ability. The English asserts that it does all three and changes the skill gap into exposing Haruki's weaknesses.
findings.japanese:
俺の音にイタズラしているようにも、
俺を導いてくれてるようにも、
腕の違いを見せつけてるようにも聞こえる、不思議な音。
findings.todokanai: It was a mysterious sound that would pull pranks on me, guide me, and even show me my weaknesses simply through hearing it.

findings.highlight: He doesn't always play the piano.
findings.evidenceJa: たまにピアノじゃないときもあるんだよな
findings.explanation: The neighboring performer has not been identified by number or gender. Japanese supplies no “he”; the scene is deliberately withholding who is playing.
findings.japanese:
「たまにピアノじゃないときもあるんだよな。
ベースだったり、ドラムだったり…」
findings.todokanai: "He doesn't always play the piano. Sometimes it's the bass, or the drums…"

findings.highlight: he caught me off guard
findings.evidenceJa: 先週はいきなりサックスが重なってきて
findings.explanation: The source only says a saxophone suddenly joined in. It does not identify a male performer.
findings.japanese: 先週はいきなりサックスが重なってきてビビったっけ。
findings.todokanai: Though last week, he caught me off guard by suddenly playing the saxophone.

findings.highlight: Seems like he's alone.
findings.evidenceJa: どれも一人でやってる感じ
findings.explanation: Haruki says each performance sounds solo, while the following narration preserves as a hypothesis whether one person plays every instrument. “He's alone” prematurely fixes both a single identity and male gender.
findings.japanese:
「さあ？
でも合わせてるの聞いたことないな。
どれも一人でやってる感じ」
findings.todokanai: "Who knows? I've never heard 'them' play together. Seems like he's alone."

findings.highlight: he intervenes when I'm alone
findings.evidenceJa: こっちが一人の時を狙って介入してくる
findings.explanation: The Japanese continues to omit the performer's identity and gender. The English repeatedly supplies a male subject.
findings.japanese:
だからこそ、こっちが一人の時を狙って介入してくる。
どうやら、よほどの暇人らしい。
findings.todokanai: Which is precisely why he intervenes when I'm alone. Seems like he has a lot of spare time.

findings.highlight: he's never missed a note
findings.evidenceJa: 向こうがミスってるのを聞いたことがない
findings.explanation: 向こう means the performer or performance on the other side; it does not establish a man.
findings.japanese:
どんな楽器でも、どんな曲でも、
向こうがミスってるのを聞いたことがない。
findings.todokanai: No matter what instrument or song, he's never missed a note.

findings.highlight: Perhaps he's had a lot of practice.
findings.evidenceJa: 練習時間が有り余ってる
findings.explanation: Haruki speculates that the unknown performer has an excess of time available to practice, continuing his “idle person” joke. The English changes available time into completed practice and again invents male gender.
findings.japanese:
…やっぱり、練習時間が有り余ってる、
よっぽどの暇人なのかも。
findings.todokanai: …Perhaps he's had a lot of practice. He certainly does seem to have a lot of spare time.

findings.highlight: There's an annex opposite of us connected by two sections where there's an extra-large third music room.
findings.evidenceJa: 向かいの新館に、こっち二つを繋げたくらいの、特大の第三
findings.explanation: The third music room is in the new building opposite and is roughly as large as Music Rooms One and Two combined. The English invents an annex physically connected by two sections.
findings.japanese:
峰城大付の音楽室は、こっちの本館に第一と第二、
向かいの新館に、こっち二つを繋げたくらいの、
特大の第三と、全部で三つも用意されている。
findings.todokanai: Houjou High School has three music rooms. Music Room 1 and 2 are here in the main building. There's an annex opposite of us connected by two sections where there's an extra-large third music room.

findings.highlight: the music students' classes, the eighth class of each grade
findings.evidenceJa: 学年８クラス中１クラスしかない音楽科専用
findings.explanation: The music course occupies one of each grade's eight classes. It is not “the eighth class” of each grade.
findings.japanese:
けれどそのうちの第二と第三は、
学年８クラス中１クラスしかない音楽科専用で、
他の部活や同好会は、狭い第一音楽室を分け合うしかない。
findings.todokanai: However, all the clubs have to share the cramped Music Room 1. Unlike the other two, which are reserved only for the music students' classes, the eighth class of each grade.

findings.highlight: We also have to think of the school's interests as well
findings.evidenceJa: 学校側も相当に力を入れてるしで
findings.explanation: The school itself invests heavily in students who plan to make a living in music. The line does not say that Haruki and the regular-course students must consider the school's interests.
findings.japanese:
まぁ、将来音楽で飯を食う野望を秘めた奴らの巣窟だし、
学校側も相当に力を入れてるしで、仕方ないんだけど。
findings.todokanai: It goes without saying that it's a haven for people who have hopes of getting into a music career. We also have to think of the school's interests as well, so there's nothing we can really do.

findings.highlight: Especially since I'm in third year already, things have gotten pretty tough.
findings.evidenceJa: 特に今年の三年はかなりレベル高いって話だし
findings.explanation: Takeya says this year's third-year music students are reputedly exceptionally skilled. The English makes the problem Takeya's own third-year status and omits their high level.
findings.japanese:
「ま、それを差し引いても望み薄だな。
特に今年の三年はかなりレベル高いって話だし」
findings.todokanai: "Well, that aside, my chances were pretty slim to begin with. Especially since I'm in third year already, things have gotten pretty tough."

findings.highlight: Maybe he's doing secret special training?
findings.evidenceJa: 秘密特訓でもしてるんか
findings.explanation: Takeya speculates about the still-unidentified person or people in the room. The Japanese does not establish a male performer.
findings.japanese:
「…えらく人見知りだな。
秘密特訓でもしてるんか？」
findings.todokanai: "…That's pretty shy. Maybe he's doing secret special training?"

findings.highlight: with him trying to hide behind the Iron Curtain
findings.evidenceJa: こうして鉄のカーテンを引かれると
findings.explanation: The passive construction says that an Iron Curtain has been drawn against Haruki, without identifying who drew it. “Him” is unsupported.
findings.japanese:
お隣さんに興味がないって言ったら嘘になる。
しかもこうして鉄のカーテンを引かれると余計にだ。
findings.todokanai: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't curious. Even more so with him trying to hide behind the Iron Curtain like he is.

findings.highlight: his piano playing
findings.evidenceJa: 素人耳には、完璧にしか聞こえないピアノ
findings.explanation: Haruki evaluates the instruments while the performer's identity remains hidden. The repeated masculine possessive is not in the source.
findings.japanese:
素人耳には、完璧にしか聞こえないピアノ。
それより少しは落ちるけど、きっちり合わせてくる
ベース、ドラム、サックス。
findings.todokanai: To an amateur such as myself, his piano playing is perfect. And although not as perfect, his bass, drums, and saxophone all hold up well.

findings.highlight: If he really is doing this all by himself
findings.evidenceJa: もし一人でやってるとしたら
findings.explanation: The source explicitly keeps it hypothetical whether a single person plays everything and supplies no gender. The English needlessly identifies that hypothetical person as male.
findings.japanese:
もし一人でやってるとしたら、ありえない多芸多才。
天才芸術家とは違うかもしれないけど、
天才芸人であることは間違いない。
findings.todokanai: If he really is doing this all by himself, he's impossibly multi-talented. Maybe not a prodigy of an artist, but certainly an amazing performer.

findings.highlight: at his home in Nishiyama
findings.evidenceJa: 西山宅でちっとも病気じゃない和司を説教してたら
findings.explanation: 西山宅 is Nishiyama's home; Nishiyama is the absent student's surname. The English turns it into a place where Kazuji's home is located.
findings.japanese:
自己満足的に熱いセッションをこなし、
西山宅でちっとも病気じゃない和司を説教してたら、
いつの間にか秋の夕暮れは赤みを消していた。
findings.todokanai: Having finished that heated session feeling satisfied with myself, and after lecturing Kazuji for not being sick in even the slightest at his home in Nishiyama, the red of the autumn evening sky had faded away before I could realize it.

findings.highlight: Despite already clearing two-thirds of your requirements
findings.evidenceJa: ３分の２は通るってのに
findings.explanation: Haruki says roughly two-thirds of applicants get the internal university recommendation. He does not say Io has personally completed two-thirds of a set of requirements.
findings.japanese:
「ああ…
そういえば、上への推薦ヤバいんだっけ？
３分の２は通るってのに」
findings.todokanai: "I see… Speaking of which, I heard you're having trouble getting a recommendation for university. Despite already clearing two-thirds of your requirements, no less."

findings.highlight: since I exceed her in both grades and grace
findings.evidenceJa: 成績や細かさで優位に立てるおかげで
findings.explanation: 細かさ is Haruki's greater fussiness, precision, or talent for picking at details—not “grace.” That mildly unflattering advantage helps him avoid feeling awkward around Io as a girl.
findings.japanese:
…なんだけど、成績や細かさで優位に立てるおかげで、
異性としての苦手意識を感じさせない貴重な友人の一人。
findings.todokanai: …Despite that, she's become an important friend of mine. Although, since I exceed her in both grades and grace, I'm not terribly conscious of the fact that she's of the opposite sex.

findings.highlight: I only look quiet
findings.evidenceJa: 比較対象のせいで朴念仁に見られるだけだ
findings.explanation: 朴念仁 here is a romantically oblivious blockhead, not a quiet person. Haruki's usual defense is that comparison with Takeya merely makes him look sexless or dense.
findings.japanese:
『比較対象のせいで朴念仁に見られるだけだ』
という、いつもなら絶対に口をついて出る弁解は、
諸般の事情を鑑みて自粛しておいた。
findings.todokanai: Usually I'd justify myself by saying, "I only look quiet because of who you keep comparing me to," but due to various circumstances, I decided to hold it in.

findings.highlight: she's way up there
findings.evidenceJa: 思いっきり身持ち固いよ
findings.explanation: Io says Setsuna is extremely guarded and respectable in relations with men. “Way up there” suggests status or unattainability while dropping the specific reason a beginner could not break down her defenses.
findings.japanese:
「それに思いっきり身持ち固いよ？
初心者に崩せる相手じゃないと思うけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "And she's way up there, you know? I don't think she's someone a beginner like you could handle."

findings.highlight: Takeya's carefree attitude has gotten him into some bad luck there.
findings.evidenceJa: 武也のいい加減な口車に乗って貧乏くじ
findings.explanation: Io says Haruki has once again drawn the short straw by falling for Takeya's irresponsible sales pitch. The English makes Takeya the victim of the bad luck.
findings.japanese:
「また武也のいい加減な口車に乗って貧乏くじ。
そろそろ学習すればいいのに」
findings.todokanai: "Takeya's carefree attitude has gotten him into some bad luck there. He should've learned his lesson already."

findings.highlight: I don't really feel it's irrational or pointless
findings.evidenceJa: そんな理不尽とやるせなさも感じないではないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki does feel the unfairness and frustration; he says he is not without those feelings. The translation negates them. It then misassigns “beyond control” to the work rather than his compulsive responsibility and meddling.
findings.japanese:
そんな理不尽とやるせなさも感じないではないけど、
それよりも湧き上がる無駄な責任感と節介癖は、
どうやら自分でも制御不能な域に達してるようで。
findings.todokanai: I don't really feel it's irrational or pointless, but even with my burning sense of responsibility and nosy tendencies, it seems that this too, is far beyond my capabilities.

findings.highlight: this is the moment where everything goes back to square one
findings.evidenceJa: 学園祭実行委員代理補佐としての目が、ふと素に帰ってしまう瞬間
findings.explanation: This is a moment when Haruki's committee-assistant perspective drops away and he suddenly returns to his unguarded personal self. Nothing goes back to square one.
findings.japanese:
そんな、学園祭実行委員代理補佐としての目が、
ふと素に帰ってしまう瞬間がある。
findings.todokanai: From the eyes of a school festival committee assistant, this is the moment where everything goes back to square one.

findings.highlight: It was a wordless remark, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: どう見ても呆れてるというか
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects himself: her look is not resentful; by any reading she is exasperated with him. The English invents a “wordless remark” and omits the actual correction.
findings.japanese:
…という意図の目つきじゃないけどな、あれは。
どう見ても呆れてるというか。
findings.todokanai: …Then again, maybe that's not what she intended. It was a wordless remark, after all.

findings.highlight: In the late autumn What goes around comes around Compassion's your call
findings.evidenceJa: 秋深し　情けは人の　ためならず
findings.explanation: This is the second parody of Basho's 秋深き／隣は何を／する人ぞ in the scene, so it should visibly recall the earlier altered haiku while splicing in the proverb 情けは人のためならず. The English neither preserves that paired literary callback nor has source support for the added phrase “Compassion's your call.”
findings.japanese: 秋深し　情けは人の　ためならず
findings.todokanai: In the late autumn What goes around comes around Compassion's your call

findings.highlight: He's here today too.
findings.evidenceJa: 今日もいた
findings.explanation: Haruki is relieved that the still-unidentified neighboring performer is present. The Japanese supplies neither name nor gender; “he” prejudges the reveal.
findings.japanese:
「…よかった。
今日もいた」
findings.todokanai: "…Good. He's here today too."

findings.highlight: a proper fine arts student
findings.evidenceJa: 単なる文章好きの文系学生
findings.explanation: Haruki describes himself as an ordinary humanities student who likes writing or literature. 文系 does not mean a fine-arts student, and “proper” is invented.
findings.japanese:
女を口説く環境作りに余念のないあいつと違って、
俺は単なる文章好きの文系学生だったから、
最初はコードの存在すら知らなかった。
findings.todokanai: While he was busy flirting with girls, I was busy being a proper fine arts student who simply enjoyed literature. Because of that, I didn't even know what chords were at first.

findings.highlight: there'd be various things that might perplex you
findings.evidenceJa: 様々な観点から総合的に評価して首を捻る程度
findings.explanation: Haruki says that even now, a comprehensive evaluation from various angles would leave him tilting his head over whether he has improved. The English transfers the perplexity to an unspecified “you” and loses the negative self-assessment.
findings.japanese:
ま、今でもそんなに上達してるかと問われれば、
様々な観点から総合的に評価して首を捻る程度だけど。
findings.todokanai: Though if you asked me right now if my playing had improved at all, there'd be various things that might perplex you.

findings.highlight: My low skill level would probably have just caused them trouble.
findings.evidenceJa: 迷惑をかけたという程には相手にされてなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says they paid so little attention to him that he did not even rise to the level of causing them trouble. The English states the opposite: that his low skill probably did burden them.
findings.japanese:
そんな適当な仲間にも、俺は全然ついていけなくて。
…迷惑をかけたという程には相手にされてなかったけど。
findings.todokanai: And I just couldn't keep up with them… My low skill level would probably have just caused them trouble.

findings.highlight: the song that I've perfected
findings.evidenceJa: 最初にトチらずに弾けるようになった曲
findings.explanation: It was the first song Haruki learned to play without making a mistake. “Perfected” greatly overstates his explicitly modest guitar ability.
findings.japanese:
俺が一番最初に練習して、
最初にトチらずに弾けるようになった曲。
findings.todokanai: This is the song I first began practicing with. And it is the song that I've perfected.

findings.highlight: getting on the bandwagon
findings.evidenceJa: ミーハーかつマイナー
findings.explanation: Takeya's label is the comic contradiction “trendy and obscure.” The English keeps only the trendy half and deletes the deliberately incompatible “minor.”
findings.japanese:
武也には『ミーハーかつマイナー』と笑われたけど、
好きなものは好きなんだから仕方ない。
findings.todokanai: Takeya laughed it off as me "getting on the bandwagon," but I can't help but like it.

findings.highlight: common for karaoke or TV programs to feature this universally beloved song
findings.evidenceJa: カラオケや有線でもある程度定番化されてて
findings.explanation: 有線 is wired music or cable radio, not television. The source calls the song a modestly, quietly loved seasonal standard; “universally beloved” also inflates its deliberately understated status.
findings.japanese:
今や、カラオケや有線でもある程度定番化されてて、
これからの季節、リクエストが徐々に増えていく、
地味に愛されてる曲。
findings.todokanai: Even now it's common for karaoke or TV programs to feature this universally beloved song, and requests for it only increase during the coming season.

findings.highlight: An artist with extraordinary abilities at the time, topping charts even in the U.S., and attaining fame worldwide.
findings.evidenceJa: 今や全米チャートにでさえ顔を出す国際的アーティストは、その頃からやっぱり実力が並外れてた
findings.explanation: Rina appears on American charts now; the retrospective point is that her ability was already extraordinary back then. The English grammar places the international chart success “at the time” of the old festival.
findings.japanese:
最優秀賞は緒方理奈。
今や全米チャートにでさえ顔を出す国際的アーティストは、
その頃からやっぱり実力が並外れてた。
findings.todokanai: The top prize had gone to Ogata Rina. An artist with extraordinary abilities at the time, topping charts even in the U.S., and attaining fame worldwide.

findings.highlight: despite knowing I was a bad singer
findings.evidenceJa: キーが合わないのを承知の上で、裏声で歌いまくり
findings.explanation: Haruki knew the song's key did not suit his voice and therefore sang it repeatedly in falsetto. The source does not call him a bad singer.
findings.japanese:
その番組を見てからしばらくは、
キーが合わないのを承知の上で、裏声で歌いまくり、
家族やクラスメートのひんしゅくを買いまくった。
findings.todokanai: After watching that show, despite knowing I was a bad singer, I kept singing the song in falsetto, bearing all the frowns from my classmates and family.

findings.highlight: despite it not really fitting the guitar
findings.evidenceJa: ギターを弾くだなんて似合わないことを始めたときも
findings.explanation: Playing guitar is what seemed out of character for Haruki. The English makes the song seem ill-suited to the instrument instead.
findings.japanese:
だから、ギターを弾くだなんて似合わないことを
始めたときも、やっぱり皆のひんしゅく覚悟で、
最初に挑む曲は決まっていた。
findings.todokanai: Which was why when I started, despite it not really fitting the guitar, and expecting everyone to frown upon it, this was the song I had decided to take on.
